section_summary: This section continues a Japanese Economic Stabilization Board analysis of the economy, documenting rising production and real wages alongside slower inflation. It then examines trade deficits, weak enterprise finances, deteriorating infrastructure and living standards, and the difficulties of stabilization, price reform, and reconstruction. The section ends with a dated title page and table of contents for the analysis.

subfiles.title: Analysis of Current Economic Situation of Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s economic stabilization, its underlying weaknesses, and the problems posed by price reform and reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Production and real wages rose in 1948 while inflation slowed, aided by better supplies, harvests, transport, and financial restraint. The report argues that import surpluses, inadequate depreciation, subsidies, damaged land and infrastructure, and low living standards undermine this apparent progress. It examines divergent domestic and international prices, weak purchasing power, hardship among farmers and smaller firms, and the need to revise economic controls. It concludes that fiscal pressures, wage increases, and reconstruction investment could renew inflation unless Japan builds a stable, self-supporting economy.
